QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H fell from 0.520 (Nov 6) to 0.454 (Nov 25), below 0.5 for ideal independent finite-variance returns. R²=0.920 measures fit only over scales 8–63. Short/long estimates (0.364/0.537) show one exponent fits poorly, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Absolute-return H=0.757 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H fell 0.026 over one observation and 0.020 over five. It was 1.79 standard deviations below its prior-30 baseline; overlapping windows make this no significance test.

Hill alpha was 3.27 on Nov 23–24, then 3.33, using 100 extremes from 1,000 returns with a 2.046% absolute log-return cutoff. Unchanged extremes can leave alpha flat. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The independent-return standard error, 0.333, understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.32/3.00, not a confidence interval. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SOXX.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:

Short/long slopes (0.389/0.482) differ: one line fits poorly across scales 8–63, possibly reflecting a crossover or temporary volatility shift.

Magnitude H=0.748 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability. H changed −0.0195 and −0.0020 over one and five observations, respectively. Its prior-30 z-score was −1.71, not a significance test because windows overlap.

Idealized independent-return SE=0.29 understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.19/2.47, not a confidence interval. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SPY.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
SPY’s 252-return DFA H was 0.478 on Nov 25, slightly below the independent, finite-variance reference of 0.5. Despite R²=0.941 on tested scales, short/long estimates (0.335/0.576) show one line fits scales 8–63 poorly, possibly reflecting crossover. Absolute-return H=0.723 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability. H fell about 0.021 over both one and five observations. The prior-30 z-score was −1.55; overlapping windows make it unsuitable for significance testing.

Hill alpha was 3.251 (1,000 returns, k=99, x_min=0.01460 in absolute log-return units). Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The independent-return standard error (alpha/√k) is 0.327, understating uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.143/2.853, not a confidence interval.

H/alpha fell from 0.527/3.400 on Nov 6. Alpha held at 3.183 Nov 23–24; unchanged extremes can produce plateaus without implying a static market. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
